recall.minute: A language model gives P(W) or P(next word); it ranks candidates in translation (high winds), spelling (minutes vs minuets) and speech (I saw a van). The chain rule is exact but long histories are unseen, so the Markov assumption keeps n − 1 words. MLE: P(w | prev) = C(prev w)/C(prev); Sam corpus P(I|<s>) = 2/3, P(Sam|<s>) = 1/3, P(am|I) = 2/3, P(</s>|Sam) = 1/2. Restaurant queries: i want .33, want to .66, to eat .28, i eat .0036, i to 0; P(<s> i want english food </s>) = .25 × .33 × .0011 × .5 × .68 ≈ 0.000031, log ≈ −10.39. Zeros (denied the offer) make sentences impossible and perplexity infinite. Add-1 with V = 1446: want|i 828/3979 = .21, to|i .00025, to|want .26, eat|to .18; c*(i want) 827 → 527, too blunt for LMs but fine for classification; add-k is gentler. Backoff uses lower orders when needed; interpolation always mixes with λs summing to 1, tuned on held-out data; stupid backoff uses 0.4 and returns scores. OOV words become <UNK>. Evaluate extrinsically or by perplexity P^(−1/N): digits → 10; newspaper text unigram 962, bigram 170, trigram 109.
